      "body": "The tag `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby: the block should close with `end`, without the trailing `if`. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The controller tests stub rendering, so they do not catch this; add a test that renders this view."
    },

      "file": "app/models/post.rb",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization on import and subsequent edits",
      "body": "Returning `raw` directly makes external HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed HTML to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. These posts are then rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Subsequent edits also retain the raw-HTML cook method, allowing an author who can edit an imported post to inject executable markup even if its initial import was safe. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before assigning their cooked content."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 48,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Automatic redirects bypass the embed host restriction",
      "body": "`TopicRetriever` checks only the hostname of the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows redirects to other hosts without repeating that check. An allowlisted URL that redirects to an internal HTTP endpoint therefore causes the worker to fetch that endpoint and potentially publish its contents as a topic. Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before connecting, or disable automatic redirects and handle them through a restricted fetcher."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb",
      "line": 35,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Feed polling assumes every entry has Atom-style content",
      "body": "Valid RSS entries can provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these entries, `i.content` is absent, so accessing it or calling `scrub` fails and aborts the entire polling run. The same exception also prevents `TopicRetriever` from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle entries without a body; test actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only delegation to `poll_feed`."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 64,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths",
      "body": "The slash-prefix rewrite treats `//cdn.example.com/image.png` as a path on the article host, producing a URL such as `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../article` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the imported article. Both anchor and image handling have this problem. Resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution instead of manually concatenating the host."
    }

findings.title: Invalid ERB Ruby prevents rendering existing discussions
findings.body: The tag `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby: the block should close with `end`, without the trailing `if`. Every embed request that finds an existing topic will fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The controller tests stub rendering, so they do not catch this; add a test that renders this view.

findings.title: Raw HTML posts bypass sanitization on import and subsequent edits
findings.body: Returning `raw` directly makes external HTML executable forum content. `PollFeed` passes feed HTML to `TopicEmbed.import`, which only parses and rewrites URLs with Nokogiri; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. These posts are then rendered as trusted cooked HTML. Subsequent edits also retain the raw-HTML cook method, allowing an author who can edit an imported post to inject executable markup even if its initial import was safe. Sanitize raw-HTML posts before assigning their cooked content.

findings.title: Automatic redirects bypass the embed host restriction
findings.body: `TopicRetriever` checks only the hostname of the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows redirects to other hosts without repeating that check. An allowlisted URL that redirects to an internal HTTP endpoint therefore causes the worker to fetch that endpoint and potentially publish its contents as a topic. Validate redirect destinations and resolved addresses before connecting, or disable automatic redirects and handle them through a restricted fetcher.

findings.title: Feed polling assumes every entry has Atom-style content
findings.body: Valid RSS entries can provide their body through `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these entries, `i.content` is absent, so accessing it or calling `scrub` fails and aborts the entire polling run. The same exception also prevents `TopicRetriever` from reaching its HTTP fallback when feed polling is enabled. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle entries without a body; test actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only delegation to `poll_feed`.

findings.title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
findings.body: The slash-prefix rewrite treats `//cdn.example.com/image.png` as a path on the article host, producing a URL such as `https://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.png` and `../article` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse page rather than the imported article. Both anchor and image handling have this problem. Resolve references against the article URL using URI resolution instead of manually concatenating the host.
